inspected_anchors.finding: Version 1.3-0, date 2023-4-13, R >=3.1.0, Matrix/matrixStats imports, optional SuperLearner and GPL-2 declaration.
Exports the simple and MSM entrypoints and censoring helpers; registers separate summary methods.
Version 1.3-0 changed deterministic-Q ordering and replaced speedglm by glm; 1.1-0 documented small-sample t intervals.
Sections0-3 distinguish running from modifying/distributing, state notice/source requirements and distinguish independent works and aggregation.
Documented column chronology, binary actions, censoring, absorbing events, outcome range and rule interface.
Default glm, cumulative gbounds .01 to1, TMLE variance; simple entrypoint constructs one or two regimes in a working model.
Single-regime output converts from logistic working parameters, preserves influence values/cumulative g diagnostics and rescales outcomes.
Creates defaults and validates input; resets unavailable requested variance method to ic, including all no-action/censoring cases.
Additional variance unavailable for nonbinary, deterministic-Q, gcomp, stratify and non-null id; warnings use selected positivity and rare-event conditions.
HouseholdIC aggregates by sum and multiplies by household/record count; FinalizeIC calls it after weighting.
Normalization uses record-level expectation matrix; near-zero rcond leads to missing matrix and a warning.
Single mean takes maximum available variance; each paired contrast applies gradients to shared covariance and selects larger available standard deviation; nonbinary RR/OR removed and scales restored.
P values switch between t with n-1 df and normal; MSM standard errors divide by number of influence rows.
Summary propagates a full covariance via gradient and divides by influence-row count; t critical value is used for n<100 and normal otherwise.
Fewer than two fitting observations stop; constant outcome skips fitting; learner calls receive weights and id; selected warnings are suppressed and some out-of-range predictions bounded.
Cumulative products are computed first, then bounded; a floor on each incremental probability is a different calculation.
Checks chronological index order and disjoint node roles and restricts CV options; accepts non-GLM library only if SuperLearner is present.
Treatment binary checks, survival consistency, NA restrictions, weight and id validation; supplying a vector id is not a sampling-law proof.
Outcome clipping/scaling and post-event/censoring cleaning; explicit range division motivates nondegeneracy validation.
Default regressions include prior nodes with exclusions for censoring, events or treatment stratification.
Numeric C=1 is uncensored; conversions precede helpers; suppresses extreme-probability/rank warnings and, in update steps, nonconvergence warning.
GLM and glm.fit helpers set maxit=100; no native convergence qualification follows.
Failed solve returns missing matrix and warning; successful return does not establish scientific identifiability.
Warning suppression uses exact warning-message match and muffleWarning.
Named is.censored/is.uncensored arguments distinguish coding and return censoring factors.
Templates must be completed; factor/index conversion and absorbing-event behavior are documented.
Separate historical implementation is marked testing-only and subset scope; it is not independent qualification.

limitations: Source-level proposal reference; no downloaded R code, package tests or external dependency was executed.
The cutoff-filtered default-branch query returns this 2023 commit. A June 2026 repository push is a separate observation; CRAN release equality and other branches are not established.
GPL-2 package declaration and authentic standard license are inspected; transitive dependency compatibility and a specific distribution arrangement remain to be reviewed.
Matrix, matrixStats, SuperLearner, R runtime and BLAS implementation versions are not locked or qualified.
Native fit behavior, dynamic-rule correctness, nuisance assumptions, positivity, cluster sampling and calibration require future matched trials.
Exact finite-law and covariance examples are authored mathematical references; they are not package execution, fitted influence values or bank returns.
The decision does not close longitudinal software coverage, grant an integration capability or accept a product.
